title: Выдуманная смерть дедушки  (The Invented Death of a Grandfather)

segments.t: Believing the guest is married to Spartak defender Makeev, Chef Barinov happily fries the tartare and asks the waiter to wish her husband luck in tomorrow's big match. Meanwhile, when Vika asks why Max did not fly to Cyprus with Sasha, Max impulsively lies that Kostya's grandfather passed away.
И передай от шеф-повара удачи мужу в завтрашнем.
А я смотрю.
А откуда ты знаешь?
Между прочим, я сам отказался лететь.
А что по этому поводу думает Саша?
А что Саша?
С Сашей у меня как бы все.
А я не мог.
Горе случилось, дед умер.
Нет, у Кости.
У тебя?
Надо было помочь другу, саму понимаешь?
Да, конечно.
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
И передай от шеф-повара удачи мужу в завтрашнем.
'And pass along good luck from the head chef to her husband tomorrow.' Notice how Russian expresses 'both' and 'tomorrow's' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
А я смотрю.
'So I see.' Kostya anchors the line on 'and', while 'look' completes the thought.
А откуда ты знаешь?
'And how do you know about that?' Notice how Russian expresses 'and' and 'know' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Между прочим, я сам отказался лететь.
'By the way, I refused to fly myself.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'refused', turning the action back on the subject.
А что по этому поводу думает Саша?
'And what does Sasha think about that?' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'and' before landing on 'Sasha'.
А что Саша?
'What about Sasha?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'and' and finishing on 'Sasha'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
С Сашей у меня как бы все.
'Things between Sasha and me are basically over.' The meaning hinges on 'with' working together with 'all' in spoken Russian.
А я не мог.
'I just could not go.' Kostya anchors the line on 'and', while 'could' completes the thought.
Горе случилось, дед умер.
'A tragedy happened, his grandfather died.' Notice the reflexive suffix on the verb meaning 'to happen', turning the action back on the subject. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Нет, у Кости.
'No, Kostya's grandfather.' Chef Viktor anchors the line on 'there is no', while 'bones' completes the thought.
У тебя?
'Yours?' Russian expresses 'having' with the preposition 'by' plus the genitive pronoun and 'you'.
Надо было помочь другу, саму понимаешь?
'I had to support pal, you understand, right?' Notice how Russian expresses 'at' and 'do you understand' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Да, конечно.
'Yes, of course.' The grammar packs 'yes' and 'of course' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.
